summary: Jan Safarewicz was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. at Vilnius University and studied at the University of Paris under Émile Benveniste and Antoine Meillet, later holding professorships at Vilnius University and Jagiellonian University.

Jan Szczepan Otrębski specialized in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Warsaw, Leipzig, and Jagiellonian University, completing his PhD under Jan Michał Rozwadowski, and held faculty positions at Vilnius University and Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań.
Jan T. Ergardt worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Rune Edvin Arvid Johansson and earned his Ph.D. from Lund University by 1970, where he is attested as a colleague in 1989.

Jan Westerhoff is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned PhDs at Cambridge under Michael Potter and at SOAS, later holding positions at Durham University and the University of Oxford, including Lady Margaret Hall.
Jan Wilhelm Boissevain was an Indologist. He completed his PhD at Leiden University by 1905 under the supervision of Jacob Samuel Speyer.

Jan Willem de Jong was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at Leiden and studied at Paris and Harvard, later working at Leiden University and the Australian National University, and founding the Indo-Iranian Journal.

Jan de Vries worked in linguistics, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Amsterdam and Leiden University, where he also studied under Willibald Kirfel, and served on the faculty at Leiden University from 1926 to 1946.

Jan van der Valk is a scholar of Tibetology and Indology. He earned an MSc in biology at KU Leuven and an anthropology PhD at the University of Kent, later serving as a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Vienna (2018–2024).

Jan-Ulrich Sobisch is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctorate under David P. Jackson. His academic appointments include positions at the University of Hamburg, University of Munich, University of Copenhagen, CERES Bochum, and Erlangen-Nuremberg.
Janakiballav Bhattacharyya was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He was a pupil of Surendranath Dasgupta and held an affiliation attested at Jadavpur University in 1977.
Janardan Mishra worked in Indology and philosophy. He served as Director of the Mithila Institute of Post-Graduate Studies and Research in Sanskrit Learning, with his post attested in 1959 and 1987.
Jane Bunnag is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of London by 1969, supervised by E. Michael Mendelson and Barbara E. Ward.
Jane Caple is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She held posts at the University of Leeds and the University of Manchester, where she is attested as a Research Fellow in 2026.

Jane Ellen Harrison was a religious studies and archaeology scholar. She studied at Cheltenham Ladies' College and Newnham College, Cambridge, under Robert Alexander Neil, and held an academic post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1898 to 1922.
Jane Helen Rowlands worked in Indology and linguistics. She studied at Bangor, Newnham College, Cambridge, Calcutta (MA), and the Sorbonne (PhD), and taught English at Karimganj College.

Jane-Marie Law is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology. She has held posts at Cornell University, serving as Director of Graduate Studies (attested 2008) and Associate Professor (attested 2026).

Janet Gyatso is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her BA, MA, and PhD at UC Berkeley and held posts at Amherst College and Harvard University, where she became Hershey Professor of Buddhist Studies in 2001.

Janet R. Goodwin specializes in Japanology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at UC Berkeley under Delmer M. Brown and Britten Dean, later holding positions at the University of Southern California and the University of Aizu, both attested in 1994.

Jang-Kil Chun is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. They completed doctoral work supervised by Minoru Kiyota, having also studied under Paul J. Griffiths, Geshe Lhundup Sopa, and Frances Wilson.

Janice Dean Willis is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned degrees at Cornell and Columbia (PhD under Alex Wayman) and served as a professor at Wesleyan University (1977–2013) and a teacher at Agnes Scott College (2014–2020).
